title: Chef-Style Tiramisu Gateau
description: Luscious layers. Boozy brilliance. A dessert that whispers Italian and screams, "I'm extra."

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 9-inch round cake tin with baking paper.
Place eggs and sugar in a heatproof bowl over a pot of simmering water. Whisk until warm and frothy.
Remove from heat and beat with an electric mixer until thick, pale, and ribbony.
Gently fold in the sifted plain flour, cornflour, salt, and vanilla. Take your time — slow and gentle keeps the air in.
Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and springy to the touch.
Cool completely in the tin, then slice into 2 or 3 even layers.
Brew 180ml of strong espresso. While still hot, dissolve 90g white sugar into it and stir well.
Reduce over low heat — barely a simmer — to approximately 200ml total volume. This takes 5–8 minutes. You are concentrating the sugar, not cooking the coffee.
Cool completely. Once cold, stir in the Tia Maria and Grand Marnier gently.
Gently whisk egg yolks and caster sugar together over a double boiler until thickened and pale — like a smooth custard. Remove from heat and cool completely.
Fold the cooled yolk mixture into the mascarpone along with the vanilla extract until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the thickened cream to soft peaks. Fold into the mascarpone mixture along with the orange zest.
Chill the mascarpone cream for 10 minutes before assembly.
Line a springform pan or cake ring with clear plastic strips for clean, professional sides. No plastic? Use baking paper — rustic is fine too.
Place the first sponge layer in the base. Brush generously with the coffee soak — bold flavour, not a coffee swamp.
Slather a thick layer of mascarpone cream over the sponge. Repeat: sponge → soak → cream.
Finish with a final generous layer of cream on top. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4–6 hours. Overnight gives the best result.
Pipe whipped cream rosettes on top, arrange fresh strawberries, and finish with white chocolate curls if using.
Use a hot, dry knife to slice cleanly. No dragging. No tears.

notes.title: Coffee Soak
notes.content: Do not boil the coffee reduction hard — you are concentrating sugar, not cooking espresso. Cool completely before adding the alcohol or you will cook off the liqueurs.

notes.title: Mascarpone Cream
notes.content: Fold, never beat. Once the cream goes in, stop as soon as it's combined — overworking it will break the texture and make it grainy.

notes.title: Sponge Soaking
notes.content: Brush the soak on — don't flood it. You want bold coffee flavour in every bite, not a soggy mess.

notes.title: Chilling
notes.content: Overnight chilling is not optional if you want clean slices and set layers. 4 hours is the minimum. Hide it behind the celery — no one will look there.

notes.title: Chef's Notes
notes.content: Tia Maria gives deep espresso elegance. Grand Marnier lifts it with sweet citrus flair. The orange zest and fresh strawberries balance the richness perfectly. This is a mousse-style gateau — airy, boozy, blissful.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days. Not suitable for freezing.
